summary: This program builds a list of Book objects and sorts it three different ways using Comparator, then uses HashSet operations to find the intersection, union, and difference between two collections of book titles.

lines.text: The wildcard import brings in every class from the java.util package, so List, ArrayList, Comparator, Set, HashSet, and Arrays are all available without separate import lines.
The variable is declared as the List interface but created as an ArrayList, which is the habit to build: code against the interface so the underlying implementation can change later.

lines.code: books.add(new Book("The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes", "Arthur Conan Doyle", "Mystery"));
lines.text: Each call creates a Book object and appends it to the end of the list, so the list keeps items in insertion order.
The enhanced for loop walks through every element of the list in order without needing an index variable.
Passing an object to println calls its toString method, which is why Book must define toString to print something readable.
Comparator.comparing builds a comparator from a key, and Book::getTitle is a method reference naming the getter that supplies that key. The sort rearranges the list in place.
Sorting by more than one field starts with the primary key, here the genre.
thenComparing supplies the tie-breaker: books that share a genre are then ordered by title.
Arrays.asList wraps the listed strings as a List, and the HashSet constructor copies them into a set, which stores no duplicates and keeps no particular order.
A copy of myTitles is made first because the set operations that follow modify the set they are called on, and the originals must stay intact for later use.
retainAll keeps only the elements that also appear in the other set, giving the titles both readers own.
addAll merges in every element of the other set, and because a set rejects duplicates the shared title appears only once.
removeAll strips out every element found in the other set, leaving the titles that are unique to your own collection.
